answer: An attacker must lock real capital across many accounts and sustain organic-looking links, making each fake identity cost a lotus of collateral plus a measurable delta in graph entropy, which peers detect and slash. Sybil resistance comes from staking a bonded deposit per identity plus a graph-based trust score: each new agent must be vouched for by an existing vertex in the trust graph, and colluding clusters are penalized when their internal edges outnumber external ones. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
